To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the transition from FFS to MMC resulted in a substantial loss in the range of services available to PLWHA; (2) the LIHP transition did not result in a loss of services; and (3) the LIHP did not result in an increase in Ryan White caseload.

(1) the number of clients served in the FFS program declined substantially, while the number served in the MMC program grew substantially; (2) the MMC program covers fewer services than the FFS program and fewer services than Ryan White; and (3) Ryan White sites are serving a large number of clients in the LIHP program.

1) the ACA will provide a significant expansion of health insurance coverage for PLWHA; 2) the transition of PLWHA to MMC has been largely successful; 3) the transition of clients to the LIHP has been largely successful, although Ryan White sites continue to serve many of the LIHP clients; and 4) the ACA implementation will be facilitated by the lessons that can be learned from the California experience.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of managed care on access to health care services and quality of care among PLWHA.
the impact of health insurance coverage on the health and well-being of persons living with HIV/AIDS.
the impact of the ACA and the LIHP on HIV/AIDS service provision in California, and the implications for the national implementation of the ACA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

(1) the ACA will expand health insurance coverage for many PLWHA; (2) the transition to managed care will require that HIV service providers continue to provide services to clients who have transitioned into managed care; and (3) Ryan White sites will need to be funded to provide these services
the California transitions to MMC and the Low Income Health Program have provided early lessons for the ACA.

(a) the LIHP has been a success in terms of the number of clients enrolled and the services they have received, but (b) it has not yet been successful in reducing the number of clients served by Ryan White sites, and (c) the LIHP may be successful in reducing Ryan White caseload only if it expands the range of services it provides.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transition to the new health care system is proceeding well.
the transition of PLWHA to MMC and the LIPH has been a success.
the Ryan White HIV/AIDS program has a critical role to play in the ACA implementation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transition to Medicaid managed care and the Low-Income health program has not reduced access to care for PLWHA.
, in the absence of a comprehensive system of care, the transition of PLWHA into managed care may not result in the expected cost savings.
the ACA transition will be a major challenge for Ryan White sites and for HIV care providers generally.
